mainTopic: Snapping fodder and spice wood on יום טוב (תיקון כלי), followed by gathering straw, producing fire, and whitening tiles
overview: The amud opens with רב יהודה's rule: animal fodder never carries a problem of תיקון כלי (preparing a utensil). רב כהנא challenges this from a ברייתא that forbids cutting spice branches. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is missing words: soft branches may be cut, and the restrictions apply only to hard ones. רב חסדא uses the same soft/hard split to settle two ברייתות that contradict each other. רב אחא בר יעקב then asks why even hard twigs should be forbidden. He points to the משנה that lets a person break a barrel to get at figs, and to רב יהודה, who snapped hard spice sticks for his students. The גמרא answers that this is a מחלוקת: רבי אליעזר forbids snapping to smell, and רבנן permit it. רב אשי explains that רבי אליעזר can accept the barrel משנה, because it speaks of a barrel already patched with pitch. The גמרא then explains three more lines of the משנה: gathering straw from the courtyard (and the argument about making piles), the ban on producing new fire, and the ban on whitening tiles. רבי יוחנן's reason for the tiles continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Animal fodder is not considered making a utensil
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's rule: trimming animal fodder never counts as תיקון כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animal fodder does not have any problem of preparing a utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יהודה's rule. Things that animals eat, like straw and soft twigs, are never treated as the forbidden act of making a utensil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals eat these materials, so they count as food, not as raw material for building tools. Shaping or trimming them is therefore not seen as making a כלי. This rule is the target of the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Preparing or fixing a utensil, which is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base rule that the whole סוגיא tests and defends.

phrases.english: Animal fodder
does not have any problem of preparing a utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹכְלֵי בְּהֵמָה אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם תִּקּוּן כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יהודה's statement from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trimming or shaping animal fodder is never considered תיקון כלי.

steps.title: רב כהנא challenges from the spice-wood teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings a ברייתא that forbids cutting spice branches, and it even makes one liable for a חטאת when cutting one to make a toothpick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא challenged רב יהודה from a ברייתא. One may move spice wood to smell it and to fan a sick person, and one may crush it in his fingers and smell it. But he may not cut it in order to smell it. If he did cut it, he is not punished, but it is still forbidden. If he cuts it to clean his teeth, he may not cut it. If he did, he must bring a חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא quotes a ברייתא about spice branches to attack רב יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spice branches are soft, and animals eat them, so they should count as fodder. By רב יהודה's rule, cutting them should be totally fine. Yet the ברייתא forbids cutting them to smell. Worse, it gives a full Torah-level penalty (חטאת) for cutting one to make a toothpick, because that is making a utensil.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him, using a תנאי source
Branches of a fragrant spice tree
He crushes or rubs it between his fingers
He cuts or snaps it off
Not punishable, but still forbidden (a rabbinic prohibition)
Liable to bring a sin-offering, which applies to a Torah-level violation

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא gives two different levels. Cutting to smell is only פטור אבל אסור. Cutting to make a toothpick is a full Torah violation (חטאת), because that turns the branch into a tool.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection to Rav Yehuda:
One may move spice-tree wood
in order to smell them,
and to wave them (as a fan) for a sick person,
and he may crush it and smell it.
But he may not cut it off in order to smell it,
and if he did cut it, he is exempt but it is forbidden.
To pick his teeth with it, he may not cut it,
and if he did cut it, he is liable to a sin-offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that animal fodder carries no problem of תיקון כלי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spice branches are a kind of animal fodder. Yet the ברייתא forbids cutting them and even makes the toothpick case a חטאת. That shows cutting fodder can be תיקון כלי.

steps.title: רב יהודה says the teaching refers to hard wood
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה admits the ברייתא contradicts him, even on the lighter ruling. So he explains that it is talking about hard branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even the ruling 'exempt but forbidden' is already hard for me. Do I even need to mention 'liable to a חטאת'? Rather, that ברייתא was taught about hard wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge. The ברייתא is not about soft fodder at all. It is about hard branches that animals do not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה first admits the problem is even bigger than רב כהנא said. By his rule, even a rabbinic ban on soft fodder makes no sense, never mind a חטאת. His answer moves the ברייתא to hard wood. Hard wood is not animal food, so his rule never covered it.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, even; used to say 'even the lesser point is a problem'
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: He (Rav Yehuda) said to him:
Now, even 'exempt but forbidden'
is difficult for me,
is it even necessary to mention 'liable to a sin-offering'?
Rather: when that ברייתא was taught, it referred to hard wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַשְׁתָּא פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר קָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is moved to hard wood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about ordinary soft spice branches, which are fodder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about hard branches, which are not fodder. So רב יהודה's rule stands.

steps.title: Can hard wood be crushed by hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that hard wood cannot be crushed by hand, yet the ברייתא allows crushing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are hard pieces of wood able to be crushed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's answer. The same ברייתא says one may crush the branch with his fingers, and that does not fit hard wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opened with 'מוללו ומריח בו', meaning he crushes it and smells it. You can only rub soft material between your fingers. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about hard wood the whole way through.

keyTerms.meaning: Able to be crushed by hand

phrases.english: Are hard pieces of wood able to be crushed?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָשִׁין בְּנֵי מְלִילָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation that the ברייתא refers to hard wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows crushing by hand, which only works with soft wood. So the whole ברייתא cannot be about hard wood.

steps.title: The teaching is missing words: soft is allowed, hard is restricted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא has words missing. Soft branches may be crushed and even cut, while the restrictions apply only to hard branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing words, and this is how it should read. One may crush it and smell it, and cut it and smell it. When is this said? With soft wood. But with hard wood, he may not cut it. If he did, he is exempt, but it is forbidden. To pick his teeth with it, he may not cut it. If he did, he is liable to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא by adding missing words. The first half is about soft branches, which are fully permitted, and the second half is about hard branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the words are filled in, the ברייתא actually supports רב יהודה. Soft branches are fodder, so one may even cut them, because there is no תיקון כלי. Only hard branches, which are not fodder, carry the ban on cutting and the חטאת for making a toothpick.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words, and this is what it teaches
In what case was this said?
To pick or clean one's teeth

steps.whatToRemember: Soft branches count as animal fodder, so one may crush them and even cut them. Hard branches are not fodder. Cutting them to smell is פטור אבל אסור, and cutting them to make a toothpick is a full חטאת, because that is making a utensil.
steps.confusionAlert: חסורי מחסרא does not mean the ברייתא is wrong. It means the wording is shortened, and the גמרא fills in the missing words so the ruling reads clearly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer turns רב כהנא's challenge into support for רב יהודה's rule about animal fodder.

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
He may crush it and smell it,
he may cut it and smell it.
In what case is this said? With soft wood,
but with hard wood, he may not cut it,
and if he did cut it, he is exempt but it is forbidden.
To pick his teeth with it, he may not cut it,
and if he did cut it, he is liable to a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 4 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Text emendation (חסורי מחסרא): the ברייתא is divided into a soft-wood case and a hard-wood case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא seemed to describe one kind of wood, so crushing and the ban on cutting appeared to apply to the same branch.
steps.terutzMaskana: Soft wood may be crushed and cut. Hard wood may not be cut: cutting it to smell is פטור אבל אסור, and cutting it for a toothpick is a חטאת. רב יהודה's rule stands.

steps.title: Two ברייתות contradict each other about snapping a twig to smell it
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא allows snapping a fragrant twig to smell it. Another ברייתא forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: a person may snap it off and smell it. Another ברייתא teaches: he may not snap it off to smell it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two ברייתות side by side, and they say opposite things. This sets up a contradiction that needs an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות talk about the same act: snapping a fragrant twig off on יום טוב in order to smell it. One says yes and one says no. The next step will have to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: He snaps it off by hand
One ברייתא teaches / another ברייתא teaches. This is the standard way the גמרא shows two sources that contradict

phrases.english: One baraita teaches:
One may snap it off and smell it,
Another baraita teaches:
One may not snap it off to smell it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא קוֹטְמוֹ וּמֵרִיחַ בּוֹ תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ לֹא יִקְטְמֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous section split soft branches from hard ones. Now a new pair of ברייתות raises the same kind of question about snapping a twig to smell it.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two ברייתות fit together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings for what looks like the same act.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the permitted case is soft twigs, the forbidden case is hard twigs
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא settles the contradiction. The permitting ברייתא is about soft twigs, and the forbidding ברייתא is about hard twigs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: There is no difficulty. This ברייתא speaks of soft twigs, and that ברייתא speaks of hard twigs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about different kinds of twigs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Snapping a soft twig is not like shaping a tool, so it is allowed. Snapping a hard twig looks more like making a usable piece of wood, so it is forbidden. This matches the soft/hard split the גמרא used earlier.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Chisda:
It is not difficult:
This one is about soft twigs,
that one is about hard twigs.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בְּרַכִּין הָא בְּקָשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא is about a different kind of twig
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be about the same twig.
steps.terutzMaskana: Soft twigs are permitted. Hard twigs are forbidden.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: why forbid hard twigs, if one may even break a barrel?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks the ban on hard twigs. He points to a משנה that lets a person break a barrel open to get at the figs inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב challenged this: With hard twigs, why not? How is this different from the משנה: A person may break a barrel to eat dried figs from it, as long as he does not intend to make a כלי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב challenges רב חסדא's answer. He asks why hard twigs should be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking a whole barrel is a bigger act of breaking than snapping a twig. Still, the משנה allows it, as long as the person is not trying to make a כלי. So snapping even a hard twig just to smell it should also be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a usable item or tool

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov challenged it:
With hard twigs, why not?
How is it different from what we learned in a mishnah:
A person may break the barrel
to eat dried figs from it,
as long as he does not intend to make a vessel!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב בְּקָשִׁין אַמַּאי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second half of רב חסדא's answer: the claim that hard twigs are forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that snapping hard twigs is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic: if breaking a whole barrel without intending to make a כלי is allowed, snapping a twig to smell it should be allowed too.

steps.title: A second challenge: רב יהודה himself snapped hard spice sticks for his students
steps.stepSummary: Two students report that רב יהודה snapped spice sticks for them on יום טוב, even though the sticks were hard enough to be ax handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: רבא בר רב אדא and רבין בר רב אדא both said: When we were at רב יהודה's house, he would snap off sticks of fragrant wood and give us stick after stick, even though they were fit to be handles for axes and hatchets.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב adds a second challenge. Real practice shows that hard spice wood was snapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood strong enough to be an ax handle is clearly 'hard'. Even so, רב יהודה snapped it so people could smell it. This contradicts the claim that hard twigs may not be snapped.

keyTerms.meaning: He snaps or breaks off branches

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: הָא רָבָא בַּר רַב אַדָּא
phrases.english: And furthermore: Rava bar Rav Adda

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: and Ravin bar Rav Adda both said:
When we were at the house of Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְפַשַּׁח וְיָהֵיב לַן אַלְוָתָא אַלְוָתָא,
phrases.english: he would snap off and give us stick after stick of fragrant wood,
even though they were fit
to be handles for axes and hatchets.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד הָא רָבָא בַּר רַב אַדָּא וְרָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same target as step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that hard twigs are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה actually snapped hard wood on יום טוב, which shows it is permitted.

steps.title: The answer: it is a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the ruling that forbids hard twigs follows רבי אליעזר. The barrel case and רב יהודה's practice follow רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this follows רבי אליעזר, and that follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחא's challenges by saying the sources follow different תנאים. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding hard twigs is the view of רבי אליעזר. The sources that permit, like the barrel and רב יהודה's practice, follow רבנן. So the contradiction is not a mistake; it reflects a real מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who is strict here
The Sages, who are lenient here

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is Rabbi Eliezer, that is the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two challenges from steps 8 and 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים who disagree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone seemed to agree about hard twigs, so the permitting sources looked like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forbidding hard twigs is רבי אליעזר's view. Permitting them is רבנן's view.

steps.title: The ברייתא about the toothpick: רבי אליעזר versus חכמים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the מחלוקת. רבי אליעזר says snapping off a toothpick is a full מלאכה. חכמים say it is only a שבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says a person may take a splinter from in front of him to clean his teeth. חכמים say he may take it only from an animal's trough. Both agree he may not snap one off. If he did snap one off to clean his teeth or to open a door with it: if he did it by mistake on שבת, he is liable for a חטאת; if he did it on purpose on יום טוב, he gets forty lashes. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. חכמים say: in both cases, it is forbidden only as a שבות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves רבי אליעזר and רבנן disagree about snapping off wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, snapping off a splinter to use as a toothpick or a key is making a כלי, a real Torah-level מלאכה. For חכמים, it is only a rabbinic שבות. This difference is the basis for the conclusion in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that snapping off the toothpick is forbidden ('ושוין שלא יקטמנו'). They disagree only about how serious it is: a Torah-level מלאכה (רבי אליעזר) or only a שבות (חכמים).

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person may take a splinter from what is in front of him
to clean his teeth with it,
and the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִטּוֹל אֶלָּא מֵאֵבוּס שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: He may take only from an animal's trough.
And they agree that he may not snap it off,
and if he snapped it off to clean his teeth with it
or to open the door with it,
if by mistake on Shabbat, he is liable for a sin-offering;

phrases.aramaic: בְּמֵזִיד בְּיוֹם טוֹב — סוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים,
phrases.english: if on purpose on Yom Tov, he receives the forty lashes;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Rabbis say:
Both this and that,
it is only forbidden as a rabbinic shevut.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר נוֹטֵל אָדָם קֵיסָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in step 10 that this is a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and רבנן disagree about how serious it is to snap off wood

steps.title: Applying the dispute to smelling: forbidden for רבי אליעזר, permitted for רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Snapping a twig to smell it is a lighter case than snapping a toothpick. So רבי אליעזר says it is פטור אבל אסור, and רבנן say it is fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר, who says there (the toothpick) that one is liable for a חטאת, would say here (smelling) that one is exempt but it is forbidden. רבנן, who say there that one is exempt but it is forbidden, would say here that it is permitted from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer. It shows how each side's view on the toothpick leads to its ruling on snapping a twig to smell it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Snapping to smell is not making a tool, so it is always one level lighter than the toothpick case. Moving down one level: רבי אליעזר goes from חטאת to פטור אבל אסור, and רבנן go from פטור אבל אסור to מותר לכתחילה. The ברייתא that forbids hard twigs follows רבי אליעזר. The barrel משנה and רב יהודה's practice follow רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the toothpick case) / here (the smelling case)

steps.whatToRemember: Snapping a hard fragrant twig to smell it depends on a מחלוקת. רבי אליעזר says it is forbidden (פטור אבל אסור). רבנן say it is fully permitted, which is why רב יהודה snapped hard spice sticks for his students.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common method of the גמרא: take each side's view in a more serious case, then move it down one level to rule on a lighter case.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּקָאָמַר הָתָם חַיָּיב חַטָּאת —
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, who says there that he is liable for a sin-offering,
here holds he is exempt but it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן דְּקָא אָמְרִי הָתָם פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר —
phrases.english: The Rabbis, who say there that he is exempt but it is forbidden,
here hold it is permitted from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּקָאָמַר הָתָם חַיָּיב חַטָּאת הָכָא פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא from step 11 and applies it to the smelling case. This completes the answer from step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For hard twigs: רבי אליעזר says snapping to smell is פטור אבל אסור, and רבנן say it is מותר לכתחילה. Each source follows one of these views.

steps.title: How does רבי אליעזר handle the barrel משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view using the משנה that allows breaking a barrel to eat its figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי אליעזר accept the משנה that says a person may break a barrel to eat the dried figs inside, as long as he does not mean to make a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר. A משנה lets you break a barrel open with no problem at all, but רבי אליעזר treats breaking things as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, רבי אליעזר said that even snapping a twig is פטור אבל אסור (no punishment, but still not allowed). Breaking a barrel seems at least as serious, yet the משנה allows it from the start. So the גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר can disagree with a plain משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he not hold / accept
To make a vessel (a usable utensil)

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Eliezer not hold
this that we learned in a Mishnah:
A person may break the barrel
to eat dried figs from it,
provided he does not intend to make a vessel?
phrases.notes: The משנה allows this from the start, not just 'no punishment.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position of רבי אליעזר that was just set out in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that breaking or snapping objects on יום טוב is forbidden (at least פטור אבל אסור).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה fully permits breaking a barrel to get food out. That seems to contradict רבי אליעזר's stricter stance.

steps.title: The barrel was already patched together
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the משנה is talking about a barrel that had already been broken and glued back with pitch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That teaching is about a מוסתקי, a barrel that was already broken and patched with pitch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רבי אליעזר. He explains that the barrel in the משנה is not a whole, solid vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוסתקי is a barrel whose pieces were already stuck together with pitch. Breaking it open again is not destroying a real complete vessel, and it does not create a new one. So even רבי אליעזר agrees it is allowed, and the משנה is no longer a problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: When that teaching was taught (it referred to...)
A broken vessel patched back together with pitch

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When that was taught,
it was about a pitch-patched barrel.
phrases.notes: It was already broken once, so it is not a real whole vessel.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר is strict about breaking things on יום טוב. The barrel משנה does not contradict him, because it speaks of a barrel that was already broken and patched.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to a special kind of barrel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows breaking any ordinary, whole barrel, which would contradict רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers only to a pitch-patched barrel (מוסתקי), which even רבי אליעזר allows breaking.

steps.title: Gathering straw from the courtyard, and the ban on piles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about gathering from the courtyard. It brings a ברייתא: you may gather, but not into piles, and רבי שמעון allows even piles.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may gather from the courtyard.' The רבנן taught: One may gather from the courtyard and light a fire, because everything in the courtyard counts as prepared. But he may not make lots of piles. רבי שמעון allows it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about gathering straw from the courtyard for fire. It quotes a ברייתא showing that the חכמים and רבי שמעון argue about making piles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things lying in the courtyard are not מוקצה. They count as מוכן (ready for use), so you may gather them for fuel. The argument is only about gathering them into neat heaps.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared, allowed to be used on יום טוב (not מוקצה)

phrases.english: "And one may gather from the courtyard."
The Rabbis taught:
One may gather from the courtyard and kindle,
for everything in the courtyard is prepared,
provided he does not make piles upon piles.
And Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְגַבֵּב מִן הֶחָצֵר. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the twig discussion and moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may gather straw from the courtyard for fire on יום טוב, but according to the חכמים not into piles. רבי שמעון allows piles too.

steps.title: What is the basis of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים and רבי שמעון are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants to know the reasoning behind each side, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that gathering is allowed. The only question is why piles should make a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: On what point do they disagree?

phrases.english: On what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָא מִפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for the dispute over making piles.

steps.title: What it looks like versus what the pot shows
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים worry that piles look like stockpiling for after יום טוב. רבי שמעון says the cooking pot shows the real purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master (the חכמים) holds: It looks like he is gathering for tomorrow and another day. The other master (רבי שמעון) holds: His pot proves what he is doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides. The argument is about how the act looks to people watching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say neat piles look like storing fuel for a weekday, and preparing on יום טוב for a weekday is forbidden. רבי שמעון answers that onlookers can see his pot on the fire, so it is obvious the straw is for today's cooking. No one will suspect him.

keyTerms.meaning: His pot proves (his intention) about him

phrases.english: One master holds:
It looks as though he is collecting
for tomorrow and another day.
And the other master holds:
His pot proves about him.

steps.whatToRemember: The argument over piles is about appearances. The חכמים worry it looks like stockpiling for a weekday. רבי שמעון says the pot on the fire shows the straw is for today.
steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: מִחֲזֵי דְּקָא מְכַנֵּיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים forbid piles because they look like preparing for a weekday. רבי שמעון permits them because the pot shows the straw is for יום טוב cooking.

steps.title: Why may one not produce fire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on producing new fire and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not produce fire,' and so on. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, which forbids making a new fire, for example by striking stones. It asks why, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking and lighting from an existing flame are allowed on יום טוב. So it is fair to ask why making a brand-new fire for cooking should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Producing (bringing out) fire, such as from stones or wood

phrases.english: "One may not produce fire," etc.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאוּר וְכוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why producing new fire is forbidden on יום טוב, when lighting a fire for cooking is allowed.

steps.title: Producing fire is creating something new
steps.stepSummary: Making a new fire counts as creating something new on יום טוב, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he is creating something new on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: making a fire from nothing is like bringing something new into being, and that is not allowed on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to do food work on יום טוב covers using a fire that already exists. Producing a brand-new flame is an act of מוליד (creating), which is a different kind of act and stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Creates, brings something new into existence

phrases.english: Because he creates something new on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מוֹלֵיד בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Producing fire is מוליד, creating something new, which is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: What is wrong with whitening tiles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ban on whitening tiles and asks what forbidden act is being done.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may not whiten tiles.' What is he doing wrong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: you may not heat tiles until they glow white in order to roast food on them. It asks what the problem is, which sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating a tile to roast food on it looks like ordinary food preparation, which is allowed on יום טוב. So the גמרא asks what extra forbidden act could be involved here.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he doing (that is forbidden)?

phrases.english: "And one may not whiten tiles."
What is he doing?
phrases.notes: Meaning: it is just for roasting food, so why is it forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְלַבְּנִין אֶת הָרְעָפִים. מַאי קָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What forbidden act is involved in heating tiles, if the goal is only to cook food.

steps.title: The case is about new tiles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה is speaking about new tiles. His reason begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Here we are dealing with new tiles, because...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts to answer by narrowing the case to brand-new tiles. The text breaks off in the middle of his reason, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'new tiles,' רבי יוחנן shows that the problem is not the roasting itself. Heating a new tile does something to the tile, and that is the forbidden act. The exact reason comes right after 'מפני' on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with (narrowing the case)

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished here. The word מפני ('because') leads into the reason, which appears on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Here we are dealing with new tiles,
because...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָכָא בִּרְעָפִים חֲדָשִׁים עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban applies to new tiles. The specific reason continues on the next amud.
